| automatic-tick-stall-2026-09-23 | committed | — | cloud_inspection | direct | Read-only boundary evidence for the reported stall. Last successful boundary: claim. First failing boundary: commit transport. cron.job_run_details shows 2017 successful runs of public.combat2_dispatch_scheduler_fire() at the intended 2s cadence from 06:52Z until 08:00:56Z, when the world went asleep (world_state.changed_at 08:00:58Z), so world wake, scheduler and dispatcher were all healthy and the node was selected by due-node discovery. The active encounter at the reported node held a present fighter and one living engaged creature and its claim was refreshed every 2 seconds (claimed tick 5 above committed tick 4), proving claim, decode and resolve succeeded repeatedly. Every dispatch attempt then returned commit_transport_error with PostgreSQL-category SQLSTATE 42703 (undefined column) at the commit stage. node_tick_commit and both installed wrappers trap all errors and return internal_failure, so a 42703 surfacing as a transport failure originates outside the PL/pgSQL body (PostgREST/pooler request handling or post-return deferred work). Ability submission did not bypass anything: it changed proposal content, so the failure is proposal-content dependent rather than input driven. Deferred-trigger candidates were inspected and release_stances_on_death is excluded (it returns before planning any statement while hp > 0). Postgres error logs for the window are no longer retained and no diagnostic recording covered it, so the exact undefined column remains unproven. Proving it requires one separately authorized bounded probe of node_tick_commit; no such invocation was performed and no gameplay row was repaired. ROOT CAUSE PROVEN 2026-09-23 (static catalog audit, no encounter touched): the missing column is character_inventory.status (equally node_ground_loot.status), referenced as NEW.status by the installed trigger function public.enforce_unique_holder_identity(), authored in migration 20260917133413_fc7e672e-18b4-4103-9e8a-40f493fa167f.sql line 99. Installed body matched repository source byte-for-byte, so this is an authored source defect and not installed drift. The function is attached to three tables of different shape (character_inventory, node_ground_loot, marketplace_listings) as DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint triggers; only marketplace_listings has a status column. PL/pgSQL resolves record field references when it prepares the entire IF expression, so "TG_TABLE_NAME='marketplace_listings' AND NEW.status<>'active' AND ..." raises SQLSTATE 42703 (record "new" has no field "status") on EVERY write to the other two tables regardless of the TG_TABLE_NAME guard. Because the trigger is deferred it fires at COMMIT, after node_tick_commit has returned, so the error escapes both wrappers' EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS handlers and reaches the worker as an unclassifiable commit transport failure. Failing branch: any proposal whose commit writes character_inventory, i.e. any tick recording weapon durability wear; proposals with no inventory write were unaffected, which is why an ability cast appeared correlated with progress. Static tests did not catch it because they assert column existence and authored SQL text, never PL/pgSQL record-field resolution against the installed table shape; the new guard closes that gap. Semantics confirmed in one single-connection transaction using only ON COMMIT DROP temp objects and a pg_temp clone, rolled back: the old expression raised 42703 at SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE, the corrected expression passed. No gameplay table was read for mutation, no public function was replaced in the probe, and all protected fingerprints (character_inventory durability, node_encounter tick/claim/state_version/status, characters hp/cp/max_cp/mp/reserved_buffs, node_creature hp/alive, node_intent, node_pending_event, node_tick_log) are byte-identical before and after. CORRECTION: forward migration 20260923084603_63ed1235-60fa-4f63-a4a6-f37673d50ae8.sql (sha256 4f30b604887f6d24e04dfc3d6cf24adfbc4a4f9676bef21076d28982872b60d4) replaces the function body only: the marketplace-only column is now read as to_jsonb(NEW)->>'status' inside the TG_TABLE_NAME branch, which resolves at runtime and is valid on every attached table. All three identity rules, the three deferred triggers, deterministic resolution, claim/commit fencing, exactly-once ticks, scheduler cadence, lease duration, WIS CP regeneration, engagement/release lifecycle, peaceful-creature visibility, movement, departures, rewards and ADM-025B are unchanged. Fail-closed assertions in the migration verify the installed body no longer references NEW.status, that character_inventory still has no status column, that marketplace_listings still has one, and that the three deferred triggers exist and are enabled. Security linter count unchanged (323, no new findings). No schema shape change, so official types were not regenerated; the Combat2 edge mirror regenerated with no diff, so no Edge Function required deployment and none was invoked. LIVE AUTOMATIC TICKS REMAIN UNVERIFIED and await Mik's manual verification after the world is reopened; the world is still asleep in maintenance with no schedules. |
